answer: Each name must produce a relic that no crowd could have chosen for it. Before a voyage to the oasis of open problems, the seat publishes its intended route and a prediction market stakes on that choice. Repeatedly guessed choices mean a copied mind and cost the seat its vote; choosing at random to hide fails the independent quality review of the finished relic. A farm with k seats must therefore field k genuinely different histories and decision processes, because every pair of routes is compared and shared training makes the whole fleet predictable at once.
